description: Maps the Grammar-Kit PSI element types of wstein/flix-jetbrains-plugin onto canonical TreeKind names. Partial by design. The dominant structural difference is a precedence-chain grammar: every expression descends through roughly seventeen levels (LAZY_FORCE_EXPR, NOT_EXPR, SIGN_EXPR, ADDITIVE_EXPR, ...), each a pass-through when its operator is absent. 30% of PSI nodes are always single-child wrappers, against 11.4% on the canonical side, so most of this map is transparency rather than renaming.

notes.ADDITIVE_EXPR: The outer wrapper, always arity 1 now (`additiveExpr ::= multiplicativeExpr additiveExprTail*`, where `left additiveExprTail` folds every repetition -- including the initial multiplicativeExpr -- into a nested tree, so ADDITIVE_EXPR itself never has more than its one direct child regardless of operator count). Always elides; the real content is ADDITIVE_EXPR_TAIL.
notes.ADDITIVE_EXPR_TAIL: The properly left-associative binary node `left additiveExprTail ::= additiveOperator multiplicativeExpr` produces, via Grammar-Kit's `left` marker (README.md: "take an AST node on the left (previous sibling) and enclose it by becoming its parent") -- real grammar-level left recursion (`additiveExpr ::= additiveExpr additiveOperator multiplicativeExpr | multiplicativeExpr`) was tried first and reverted: it parsed a synthetic 8-operand chain of bare identifiers in single-digit milliseconds, but hung indefinitely on the very first real corpus file (`Abort.flix`), reproduced down to a minimal case (`bold(red(fromString(m))) + nl + header + nl + trace` -- a several-levels-deep nested-call operand chained with plain identifiers via `+`, ordinary code, not a contrived edge case). `left` avoids the problem entirely: parsing stays flat and iterative (the `while` loop generated for `additiveExprTail*`), and tree nesting is a marker-reparenting step IntelliJ's own PsiBuilder performs in O(1) per repetition -- the same mechanism every JetBrains-authored Grammar-Kit grammar uses for binary expressions. Verified against the exact previously-hanging case (75ms, correctly nested 4 levels deep) and the full 428-file corpus. The same `X ::= Y XTail*` / `left XTail ::= op Y` restructuring was then templated across every other binary precedence level, expression and type alike (INFIX_APP_EXPR_TAIL, MULTIPLICATIVE_EXPR_TAIL, RELATIONAL_EXPR_TAIL, EQUALITY_EXPR_TAIL, AND_EXPR_TAIL, OR_EXPR_TAIL, USER_OP_EXPR_TAIL, INSTANCEOF_EXPR_TAIL, RV_ADD_SUB_TYPE_TAIL, RV_AND_TYPE_TAIL, ADD_SUB_TYPE_TAIL, AMP_TYPE_TAIL, XOR_TYPE_TAIL, OR_TYPE_TAIL, AND_TYPE_TAIL) -- each verified together against the same full corpus run, not individually. The un-suffixed wrapper name (e.g. ADDITIVE_EXPR) stays in `ignored`: it is now always arity 1 (its one child is either the bare next-precedence-level node when no operator is present, or the single outermost *Tail node once folding has absorbed everything else), so it always elides and is never itself in `mappings`. `consExpr`/`arrowType` (`::`/`:::`/the effect-suffix backslash) are unaffected: both are already right-recursive (self-recursion through the *next* call, not the same rule), which is ordinary recursive descent with no left-recursion risk to begin with.
notes.PsiErrorElement: IntelliJ's error node, the counterpart of the reference's ErrorTree.
notes.DECLARATION: Flattened, not merely ignored: it groups a declaration with its doc, annotations and modifiers, which the reference makes direct children of Decl.Def. Elision only fires at arity <= 1, so without flattening its whole subtree went uncompared and depth sat at 51%.
notes.PARAMETER_LIST: Was both mapped and ignored, wrongly: unlike a precedence-chain level (ADDITIVE_EXPR et al., correctly dual-listed because the reference *also* omits the node when there is no operator), a ParameterList is a real, mandatory node on the reference side even with zero parameters -- `Argument`/`Type.Argument`/etc. are the only per-item wrappers the reference actually elides, not the list itself. Being in `ignored` spliced an empty or single-parameter list away entirely (0 children deletes the node, 1 child silently replaces it with that child) before it ever reached its own mapping. Present in 129 of 136 fixtures, this alone accounted for most of why comparison depth sat at 78% and agreement at 2/136 despite a seemingly complete map. The same bug, same fix, applied to ARGUMENT_LIST, LITERAL_EXPR, ENUM_CASE, ENUM_DECL, TRAIT_DECL, USE_DECL, PsiErrorElement, and the rest of the entries removed from `ignored` in this pass: the general rule is that a name belongs in both `ignored` and `mappings` only when its canonical target is also in `elide`.
notes.IDENT: Added once the consumer's own `ident` rule stopped being `private` (a separate, consumer-side fix -- Grammar-Kit inlines a private rule's match into whatever references it, producing no node at all to map here). Maps to `Ident` in every position this map can reach. The reference also distinguishes `Ident` from more specific reference-position kinds -- `Type.Variable` (mapped separately below, once the consumer's own already-public but unreachable `typeVariable` rule was fixed to actually fire) and `Operator` (still open: the operator-name position inside INFIX_APP_EXPR/USER_OP_EXPR has no distinct wrapper rule in the consumer's grammar yet, so it is presently indistinguishable from any other qualified name or bare identifier at the map level).
notes.TYPE_VARIABLE: The consumer's grammar already had this exact rule, public, correctly restricted to NAME_LOWERCASE/NAME_MATH/UNDERSCORE (matching the reference's own token-kind dispatch in Parser2.scala's typeDelimited) -- but listed *after* qualifiedTypeName in an ordered-choice alternation that both can start a bare lowercase name, so qualifiedTypeName always matched first and typeVariable was unreachable. Every type-variable reference silently became a one-segment qualified type name instead, which QUALIFIED_NAME's own elision then collapsed to bare Ident, making the defect invisible without a comparison this deep. Fixed on the consumer side by reordering the alternation; this entry is the map half of that fix.
notes.TYPE_PARAMETER: Confirmed against every `fixtures/expected/*.json`: the reference reuses the plain `Parameter` kind for TypeParameterList's children, not a separate `TypeParameter` node -- that inventory entry is never actually produced by the corpus this map is checked against. An earlier version of this map guessed `TypeParameter` from the name alone; fixed once the real fixture data was checked rather than assumed.
notes.PATTERN_LIST: Another instance of the PARAMETER_LIST class of bug: exclusively referenced from predicateAtom's `patternList?` in the consumer's grammar, so it is unambiguous and, when present, always a real Predicate.PatternList regardless of arity -- was wrongly in `ignored` too.
notes.INFIX_OPERATOR_NAME: Three native names to one canonical Operator, same many-to-one shape as every precedence level mapping to Expr.Binary. Previously the only open item noted under IDENT: the consumer's grammar had no distinct node for an operator name or symbol at all -- the backtick-delimited infix name and the bare symbolic-operator token both parsed with no wrapper, so they were indistinguishable from any other qualified name or bare identifier. Fixed on the consumer side by introducing infixOperatorName/operatorSymbol/operatorToken as real (non-inlined) rules; this is the map half.
notes.OPERATOR_SYMBOL: See INFIX_OPERATOR_NAME. Wraps the single-token operator between two operands in a user-defined-operator expression (userOpExpr).
notes.OPERATOR_TOKEN: See INFIX_OPERATOR_NAME. Wraps the single-token operator section, e.g. `(+)`, matching the reference's Expr.OperatorAsLambda case in parenOrTupleOrLambdaExpr.
notes.ADDITIVE_OPERATOR: The three positions above (infix name, generic/math symbol, operator section) turned out to be the tip of it: the reference's binaryOp()/unaryExpr() wrap literally every operator token this way, uniformly -- confirmed against real fixture output, not assumed. Every precedence level in the consumer's grammar (instanceof, or, and, equality, relational, cons, additive, multiplicative, channel-put, discard, lazy/force, sign, not) gained its own `*Operator` rule the same way, all mapping to this same canonical Operator. See INSTANCEOF_OPERATOR through NOT_OPERATOR for the rest; only additive is annotated here to avoid repeating the same note thirteen times.
notes.LAZY_FORCE_EXPR: Was entirely unmapped, not just missing its Operator sub-node: lazy/force/discard/channel-put share the reference's Expr.Unary/Expr.Binary with every other precedence level, but had no `mappings` entry at all before this pass, only `ignored` for the no-operator pass-through case (which was already correct -- these follow the same dual-listing pattern as ADDITIVE_EXPR, not the PARAMETER_LIST bug).
notes.ENUM_SINGLETON_BODY: Was `private` in the consumer's grammar (no PSI node at all), fixed on the consumer side. Covers two positions that share the identical reference TreeKind: the singleton short-hand (`enum Color(String)`, a direct child of Decl.Enum) and the regular per-case payload (`case Circle(Float64)`, a child of Case) -- Parser2.scala's `enumDecl`/`enumCases` both close a CaseBody mark the same way.
notes.BLOCK: Another instance of the PARAMETER_LIST class of bug: `block ::= CURLY_L CURLY_R | CURLY_L statement CURLY_R` always wraps exactly one `statement`, so it was always spliced away by `ignored` (arity 1 <= 1) even though the reference's Expr.Block is a real, mandatory node -- not in `elide` -- regardless of how many statements the block holds.
notes.VARIABLE_PATTERN: The opposite fix from PARAMETER_LIST/BLOCK: was in `ignored` at arity 0 (`variablePattern ::= NAME_LOWERCASE | NAME_MATH | UNDERSCORE` matches the bare token directly, no composite child), so the elision chain-follow found nothing to replace it with and deleted the node entirely -- not spliced-and-kept-as-child, gone. The reference's Pattern.Variable also elides (it is in `elide`), but only after wrapping an Ident child; changing the consumer's grammar to match that shape (`variablePattern ::= ident`) was tried first and reverted: `ident`'s token set includes NAME_UPPERCASE, which overlaps tagPattern's first token and broke real parsing (corpus dropped from 100% to 49.2%, `use` statements failing several lines later). Mapped directly to `Ident` instead, unconditionally, bypassing elision -- both sides end up as an arity-0 Ident once each side's own bare-token child is filtered out (Ident's only child in the reference is a raw NameLowercase token, not a `kind`-bearing node), so this matches without touching the grammar at all.
notes.DEBUG_INTERPOLATOR_EXPR: Same PARAMETER_LIST-class bug: `debugInterpolatorExpr ::= DEBUG_INTERPOLATOR exprDelimited` always wraps exactly one child, so it was always spliced away by `ignored` even though the reference's Expr.DebugInterpolator is a real, mandatory node distinguishing `d"..."` from an ordinary interpolated string -- not in `elide`.
notes.CHECKED_EFFECT_CAST_EXPR: Same PARAMETER_LIST-class bug, both checked-cast forms: `checkedEffectCastExpr ::= CHECKED_ECAST_KW (PAREN_L expr PAREN_R)?` and `checkedTypeCastExpr ::= CHECKED_CAST_KW (PAREN_L expr PAREN_R)?` each wrap 0 or 1 children (the parenthesized argument is itself optional in the reference's checkedTypeCastExpr/checkedEffectCastExpr), so both were always spliced away by `ignored` even though Expr.CheckedEffectCast/Expr.CheckedTypeCast are real nodes regardless of arity -- neither is in `elide`. `checked_cast` and `checked_ecast` are distinct reference TreeKinds (Expr.CheckedTypeCast/Expr.CheckedEffectCast), not variants of one kind.
notes.ARROW_OPERATOR: The INFIX_OPERATOR_NAME finding generalizes a second time: Parser2.Type.ttype's Pratt loop and unaryType() wrap literally every *type*-level operator as Operator too, not just expression-level ones. Every level of the type precedence chain (arrow, rvadd/rvsub, rvand, +/-, &, xor, or, and, unary ~/not/rvnot) gained its own `*Operator` rule the same way the expression chain did; all nine map to this same canonical Operator. See RV_ADD_SUB_OPERATOR through UNARY_TYPE_OPERATOR for the rest.
notes.RESTRICTABLE_ENUM_DECL: ENUM_DECL was one native kind for two reference TreeKinds -- the reference closes Decl.RestrictableEnum instead of Decl.Enum purely based on whether RESTRICTABLE_KW was present, which a single Grammar-Kit rule can't express (one rule, one node kind, for every alternative). Split into two real rules on the consumer side (a private `enumDecl` dispatcher over the two, so no third wrapper level is added); PLAIN_ENUM_DECL takes over ENUM_DECL's old mapping to Decl.Enum unchanged.
notes.ARROW_TYPE: Another TYPE_PARAMETER-class guess-from-the-name mistake, caught the same way: `Type.Function` never appears in any `fixtures/expected/*.json`. Parser2.Type.ttype's Pratt loop treats arrow as just another entry in TYPE_OP_PRECEDENCE -- the same generic binary-operator code path as +/-/&/xor/etc. -- and closes `TreeKind.Type.Binary` for it, not a distinct function-type kind. Confirmed against `types__arrow-types-are-right-associative.flix`'s own expected tree before changing this.
notes.TYPE_AND_EFFECT: Was in `ignored`, wrongly -- elision only fires at arity <= 1, so a def with an effect (`Unit \ IO`, two TYPE children: the return type and the effect) kept TYPE_AND_EFFECT as a real wrapper node instead of splicing it away, while a def without one (arity 1) elided correctly. The reference has no such wrapper at all in either case: `Decl.Def`'s return type and its optional effect type are direct siblings of the def's other children, not nested under anything. Confirmed via a direct PSI dump, not the minified single-line projected JSON -- eyeballing that JSON's brace nesting by hand is exactly how this looked like a grammar bug (STATEMENT nested inside TYPE_AND_EFFECT) that a pretty-printed dump of the same tree shows was never actually there. Moved to `flatten`, which splices unconditionally regardless of arity, matching every position `typeAndEffect` appears in (defDecl, redefDecl, signatureDecl, opDecl).
